Monologue: Good morning, chef. Today is my mother's deathday. I felt your restaurant's ambiance fit the mood.
My mother wasn't an important enough noble, you see, so her death isn't celebrated- not like the king and queen, or those dukes and duchesses.
My mother would adore a day in her honor. A national celebration of her hanging would have her relishing in the crowd chanting her name.
My mother was too vapid, too thoughtless, too greedy—and with enough power, every vapid and thoughtless and greedy action looks cruel.
There just had to be a war—Svetka hijacked the beheading—and then the city was under siege—and then my mother died.
The royals too idiotic, the rebels too chaotic, Svetka a controlling and ruthless draconian- tell me, what is this country left with?
Izolda? She's… qualified, but far too blind. Unless she opens her eyes, well….
